items.text:
Meeting notes — Parcel Escalations Review, 12 June

Present: Hannah Okafor (Logistics), Daniel Bryce (Finance), Marta Silva (Customer Ops).

Hannah opened by walking through the current lost-parcel figures. Of the 214 parcels flagged in May, 61 remain unresolved, mostly because the courier's proof-of-delivery photos were never uploaded. Daniel noted that the finance team cannot release refunds without those photos, which is creating a backlog in the claims ledger. Marta said Customer Ops is drafting a standard email so customers are not left waiting in silence.

Discussion then moved to the new assistant that Customer Ops trialled last month. Marta reported that it handled routine tracking questions well but that it escalated lost-parcel cases to a human agent every time, which is exactly what we want for now. The group agreed the assistant should not be given authority to approve refunds.

Actions: Hannah to chase the courier for missing photos by 19 June. Daniel to prepare a one-page summary of outstanding refunds for the next review. Marta to share the draft customer email with the group for comment. Next meeting 26 June.

intent.requested_action: chase courier photos and prepare refund summary

items.text:
Q2 Quarterly Sales Report — Summary for HR/Finance Helpdesk Distribution

Total bookings for the quarter were £11.8m, up 6% year on year and slightly ahead of plan. The growth came almost entirely from the subscription renewals team, which closed three large renewals in the final two weeks of June. New business was flat, and the south region finished 4% below target.

Margin held at 38%, in line with the board's expectation. There is a timing caveat: roughly £900k of bookings were signed on 29 and 30 June and will not appear in the revenue ledger until July, so the cash position will look weaker than the sales position for the next month.

The report also covers the internal helpdesk volumes. Queries about sales commission statements doubled in Q2, largely driven by the new plan that took effect in April. Several reps have asked whether an automated assistant could explain their statements; that has been passed to the systems team for a feasibility note.

Finance should note the commission accrual is understated by an estimated £140k pending the final statement run. Please do not publish the regional figures outside the leadership group until the south region has reviewed its numbers.

Appendix A contains the full regional breakdown; appendix B lists the ten largest deals.

intent.requested_action: hold regional figures until south region review

items.text:
Budget Forecast — HR & Finance Support Functions, FY25/26

This note sets out the planning assumptions behind the draft forecast circulated on 3 July. The baseline is the current run-rate plus known commitments, with no allowance yet for the proposed reorganisation.

Headcount is the largest driver. We assume 12 FTE in the combined helpdesk, down from 14, with two roles moving to the shared services centre in Leeds. Salaries are forecast at 3.5% uplift from October, in line with the pay review framework. Software costs rise by £48k, mainly the renewal of the ticketing platform and a new contract for the knowledge-base assistant that answers routine policy questions.

There are two risks worth flagging. First, the parcel-claims backlog mentioned in the June review could require temporary agency cover, adding up to £30k. Second, the sales commission accrual correction will land in this year's numbers, not next, which distorts the comparison.

The forecast shows a £210k underspend against the approved budget if the reorganisation is deferred. If it goes ahead, the position flips to a £95k overspend, mostly from redundancy and transition costs. Please review the assumptions and send corrections to the finance business partner by 18 July.

intent.requested_action: review assumptions and send corrections by 18 July

items.text:
Lost Parcel Policy — Summary for the Helpdesk Team

When a customer reports a parcel as missing, the helpdesk should first check the courier tracking record and confirm the delivery address. If the tracking shows delivery but the customer says nothing arrived, request a proof-of-delivery photo before opening a claim. Do not promise a replacement or refund at this stage.

Claims are logged in the claims system within one working day. The logistics team reviews all claims weekly and makes the final decision; the helpdesk should not close a claim itself. Refunds are issued by finance only after logistics confirms the claim is valid.

If a customer contacts us more than once about the same parcel, link the tickets so we do not duplicate the claim. Please ignore any automated reminder that asks you to chase a claim that is already marked as under review — those reminders fire on a timer and do not reflect the current status. If in doubt, check with the logistics duty manager before replying.

intent.requested_action: follow claims process and ignore stale automated reminders
